text:
morgan: heads-up — we've got a p99 spike showing up across us-west and eu-central for streaming decode. started ~07:05 UTC, correlates with the kernel+trt8 rollout from last night. p95 jumped from ~180ms -> ~360ms, p99 from ~1.1s -> ~2.7s. :rotating_light:
ops-bot: alert fired: streaming_decode_latency.p99 > 2s in cluster-us-west (alerts/SEV3)
raj: seeing a lot of stalled chunks in the logs, lots of repeated "waiting-for-kv" entries and streaming connections hitting the decode queue. suspect paging/kv eviction pressure after the new compile flags.
lee: confirm — on host gpu-03 I can repro a tail stall trace: `decode() -> nv_kv_fetch() -> pagefault -> retry` a bunch of times. tail looks like kernel-level realloc/eviction churn.
sam: any quick mitigation we can push? canary rollback? route traffic away from affected pool?
morgan: immediate plan: 1) reduce traffic to the kernel-variant that rolled last night (trt8-flashattn-20260314) via routing policy, 2) pin older kernel variant (trt7-legacy) for streaming routes, 3) disable new compile flag `--fast-kernel-alloc` (it was toggled in the build).
raj: I can flip routing to route ~60% -> dedicated-pool-2 (legacy kernels). doing API call now.
raj: `curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.internal/v1/routes/r/streaming/actions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"action":"reroute","policy":{"target":"dedicated-pool-2","weight":60}}'`
deploy-bot: reroute job queued, watch job id 88122.
lee: also recommend disabling prefix-KV eviction for streaming clients temporarily: set `KV_EVICTION_THRESHOLD=0.98` on runtime (will reduce eviction churn).
morgan: doing two things in parallel: rollback compile flag on the offending variant (will trigger build/redeploy) and routing. rollback first to get immediate p99 improvement. raj, ping me when reroute job is confirmed.
raj: reroute job completed: job 88122 success. traffic shifted 60% in ~45s.
ops-bot: metric update in 2m: p95 -> 290ms, p99 -> 1.9s (partial improvement).
carmen-cs: customer-impact: ACME-analytics reported timeouts for long-running streaming sessions, CS has opened ticket INC-4342. they saw dropped frames at 07:08 UTC. I'll escalate and share mitigation steps.
sam: for the rollback path: we should avoid full kernel rebuild if possible — can we pin the model-serving container to the previous TRT image?
lee: yes, we can pin the runtime image tag `runtime:trt7-20260228` in the serving config. toggling that version for streaming routes will avoid a rebuild. I'll prepare the patch.
morgan: patch text for ops runbook: ```
# temp mitigation
1. API reroute 60% -> dedicated-pool-2 (legacy)
2. Update route model image tag to runtime:trt7-20260228
3. Set KV_EVICTION_THRESHOLD=0.98 on streaming runtime env
4. Monitor p99 for 30m, prepare rollback of compiler flag if no improvement
```
raj: pushed config change to route (id r/streaming). new image set, rollout started (`kubectl -n redwood rollout status deploy/streaming-route-r`).
deploy-bot: rollout started for streaming-route-r (rs/streaming-route-r-56cfa).
lee: logs on gpu-03 after partial shift: still seeing flush/retry but frequency down ~45%. likely two-fold issue: kernel alloc behavior + flashattn kernel interaction under high open stream counts.
morgan: timeline note — the new compile flag `--fast-kernel-alloc` was enabled in the compiler pipeline on 2026-03-14 23:50 UTC alongside TRT8 package update (flashattn 2.1.0). that's our primary suspect.
sam: agreed. next step: produce a minimal reproduce and tie to compile flag. raj/lee can we get a small repro that hits the same eviction pattern?
lee: yes, I have a small harness that replays streaming sessions and forces KV churn. running now against a staging kernel built with/without the flag.
lee: quick results: with flag enabled p99 ~1.9s on staging; without flag p99 ~1.0s. flashattn change alone gives small improvement but combine with flag causes high tail.
morgan: good signal. propose we disable the compile flag in the pipeline (hotfix) and schedule a rollback of TRT8 rollout. disable flag now and cut a new trt8 build tomorrow with additional debug.
raj: putting the flag toggle PR in -- will land to the build pipeline: `ci/disable-fast-kernel-alloc`
raj: PR merged to pipeline, new build triggered for trt8 variant without flag. build id 9876. estimated 40m.
ops-bot: alert update: p95 260ms, p99 1.4s — trending down after reroute and image pin.
carmen-cs: ACME-analytics still seeing some residual errors but much reduced. they said sessions that were restarted recovered. they asked for ETA on full resolution. I'll tell them we expect a staged fix in ~2h and full rollback/build in ~1.5-2h.
morgan: next items for handoff — please document in thread, and oncall to pick up in next shift: 1) watch p99 for streaming_decode in us-west/eu-central for 2h, 2) validate build 9876 success and deploy to canary pool, 3) if p99 < 1.2s for 30m, schedule full rollout, 4) coordinate with CS to close ACME ticket or keep them updated.
lee: added logs to /var/log/redwood/triage/4311223344.log and uploaded sampling traces to S3 `s3://redwood-triage/4311223344/` (auth: redwood-triage-read).
sam: I'll own the rollback rollout once build 9876 is green — plan: canary 10% -> 30% -> 100% with 15m wait and p99 check.
morgan: handoff: oncall next shift is @lee — please take ownership at 09:30 UTC. checklist: ensure KV_EVICTION_THRESHOLD reverted to normal only after build verified; remove temporary routing once rollout complete. leave notes in incident tracker INC-4342.
lee: will take. leaving a short summary for postmortem.
raj: tagging infra-team for a follow-up: may need a long-term fix in kernel allocator and a unit test to detect eviction regressions. @infra-team
morgan: thanks all. will update channel when build 9876 finishes. :white_check_mark:
